baseline_reproduction.method: Real server/client and forwarded TCP echo. Close the user, hold the client relay at its EOF trace hook, then cancel the client and assert Start remains blocked until that registered worker is released. The log hook changes no I/O or payload.

behavior: Attempt.WaitStopped is optional. The chain cancels the candidate first, then joins it before replacement or return, including a single-candidate chain.
Joined candidates omit the old fixed three-second grace period. Callers without a join callback, including the server listeners, retain their existing grace period.
Lifecycle.WaitStopped waits for the owner context, serializes with reconnect, seals the generation, closes its control connection, joins registered workers and clears its published status/peer/pool.
Deterministic virtual-clock tests hold teardown across a candidate replacement and assert the next candidate cannot start early; a joined candidate also avoids a synthetic one-hour grace period.
A separate held reconnect test proves final shutdown cannot complete before the reconnect releases ownership, and no new generation starts after parent cancellation.

checks: New lifecycle/chain regressions passed 20 repetitions with temporary Windows socket compilation shims outside the repository.
Full chain suite passed three repetitions locally; selected client transport regressions passed three repetitions.
Linux-targeted repository-wide go vet and staticcheck passed.

limitations: The full client application package cannot compile natively on this Windows host because adaptive.StartClient is Linux-specific. Its new real-tunnel regression was cross-compiled and run natively on Linux.
The broad client transport suite has existing Windows CRLF/source-guard failures; targeted behavior tests were used.
No race-enabled run was performed in this cross-compilation environment.
The real regression deliberately holds cleanup at a logging hook to make ownership ordering observable; it is not a throughput, WAN latency or typical shutdown-duration benchmark.
This joins registered generation workers and closes their owned sockets; it is not a claim that every unrelated runtime, metrics, external helper or third-party library goroutine has been joined.
A non-cooperative registered worker can delay final shutdown; the contract intentionally waits for actual completion instead of declaring success early.
Native restart tests covered TCP, TCPMux, WS, WSS, WSMux, WSSMux, KCP and QUIC. Raw-socket and isolated-network-namespace transports were not exercised.
Dependency versions, encryption, wire negotiation, buffering and normal stream I/O are unchanged. No general throughput, CPU or memory reduction is claimed.

Tests ran under GOMAXPROCS=2 and nice priority in isolated temporary files. Source/archive/executable hashes were verified before execution. All temporary directories were removed from both hosts; no production service or global kernel policy changed.
